lines: +Responds with an early 404 error for requests whose path cannot match any page route, without loading the Vue app, its plugins or middleware on the server.

+Page routes (including aliases) are compiled into a static route matcher at build time, and incoming requests are checked against it before server-side rendering begins. Requests that cannot match any page skip loading the app entirely and go straight to the error page.

+Requests without an `Accept: text/html` header (API clients, most scanners) receive a JSON error without loading the app at all. HTML requests still server-render the error page. A [`cache` route rule](/docs/4.x/guide/concepts/rendering#hybrid-rendering) covering the path advertises its `maxAge` as `Cache-Control` on GET/HEAD misses too, letting a CDN absorb repeat requests for unknown paths.
+This is opt-in because it can break apps that rely on runtime routing:

+- pages added dynamically with `router.addRoute()` in a plugin. To surface this early, `addRoute` is removed from the type of the router returned by [`useRouter`](/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-router) when the option is enabled.
+- route middleware that redirects unknown paths to existing pages

+The option is disabled automatically in development, when `hashMode` is enabled, when a root-level catch-all page (such as `pages/[...slug].vue`) matches every path, and when a custom `app/router.options` file may modify `routes` (a file whose default export is a plain object without a `routes` key remains compatible).
Enables the experimental [`<NuxtClientFallback>`](/docs/4.x/api/components/nuxt-client-fallback) component for rendering content on the client if there's an error in SSR.
